description: Development split for benchmark A (historical retrieval). Used for tuning representation/ranking before the held-out run. See bench/protocol.json for the frozen protocol this dataset is evaluated under.

cases.query: Users on a flaky connection keep getting the same chat message twice after they reconnect. When did we fix that?
expectedEvidence: src/relay/socket-pool.js: add() guarded with a has() check so resubscribing does not duplicate the socket.

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: Add jitter to the presence heartbeat timer
whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.reason: Touches timing of heartbeats, not message delivery duplication.

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: Avoid double-logging connection events
whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.reason: Deduplicates console log lines, not chat messages sent to sockets.

cases.query: It looks like we are hitting the token endpoint several times for what should be a single outbound call when a request retries. Was that ever fixed?
expectedEvidence: src/retry/retry-policy.js: token fetch cached for the duration of a single run() call instead of refetched per attempt.

cases.query: Why do we keep this branch that treats an empty access token as needing reauth instead of just erroring?
expectedEvidence: Commit message: the legacy-tenant IdP returns access_token: "" (not null/missing) when consent has expired; do not remove until the legacy-tenant migration completes.

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: Add retry with jitter to the OAuth token exchange call
whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.reason: A transport-level retry helper; does not explain the empty-token response branch at all.

cases.query: Why do we still send the old V1 request signature header to Acme alongside V2?
expectedEvidence: Commit message: Acme's merchant-facing dashboard, used by a dozen large customers, still only checks the V1 signature; keep both until their dashboard is confirmed updated.

cases.query: Before the push-based fan-out, how did the relay used to get messages out to sockets?
expectedEvidence: src/relay/polling-dispatcher.js (removed): polled every socket pool on a 250ms timer to flush queued messages.

cases.query: What did the job queue look like before it was rebuilt around a worker pool?
expectedEvidence: src/queue/array-queue.js (removed): plain in-process array drained by a single setInterval loop, no concurrency.

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: Refactor counters into a class for testability
whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.reason: A cosmetic metrics refactor, not a removed queue implementation.

cases.query: Why did we stop using Redis for the batch processing lock?
expectedEvidence: Commit message: incident INC-1142 -- a Redis primary failover let a second worker acquire the "same" lock and double-process a batch; Postgres advisory locks live in the same transaction as the write.

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: Increase the Redis session-cache read timeout to 200ms
whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.reason: Touches a completely different Redis-backed component (a read cache), not the batch lock.

cases.query: Why did the customer export move away from building one big CSV string in memory?
expectedEvidence: Commit message: buildCsv() OOM'd the export worker on the "all customers" report past ~4M rows; streaming NDJSON holds constant memory.

cases.query: AuthSessionProvider refreshSession
expectedEvidence: refreshSession() added to AuthSessionProvider.

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: AuthSessionProvider: cache getSession() results for 30s
whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.reason: Same class, but adds caching, not refreshSession().

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: Emit a metric from AuthSessionProvider on cache miss
Add dispose() to AuthSessionProvider to clear its cache

cases.query: AuthSessionProvider caching TTL
expectedEvidence: getSession() results cached for 30s (CACHE_TTL_MS) in AuthSessionProvider.

cases.query: Why did we drop support for Postgres 13?
expectedEvidence: Commit message: pg_advisory_xact_lock + parallel-worker interaction was only fixed in Postgres 14, and staying on 13 would reintroduce the duplicate-processing bug the locking migration just fixed.

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: Document Postgres 15 compatibility in the ops runbook
whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.reason: Mentions a different Postgres version and is documentation-only, not a support drop.

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: Require Node 20; drop support for Node 18
whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.reason: A version drop in a completely different runtime (Node, not Postgres).

cases.query: Why do we now require npm 9 or newer to work on this project?
expectedEvidence: Commit message: the lockfile moved to lockfileVersion 3, which npm 7/8 silently rewrite to v2 on install, diverging from CI.

cases.query: Where did the old dispatch.js fan-out logic move to?
expectedEvidence: src/relay/dispatch.js renamed to src/relay/fanout.js, single-change rename.

cases.query: Whatever happened to the RetryPolicy class — is it called something else now?
expectedEvidence: src/retry/retry-policy.js (RetryPolicy) renamed to src/retry/idempotent-retry-policy.js (IdempotentRetryPolicy).

cases.query: Find the change that stopped a room's "user joined" listener from being wired up more than once.
expectedEvidence: src/presence/tracker.js: markOnline() now tracks a per-room listener ref count so the listener is only attached once (subject was just "fix issue").

cases.query: Something stopped the worker pool from ever running more jobs at once than its configured size allows -- which commit?
expectedEvidence: src/worker/pool.js: release() guarded against going below zero, which had let busy drift negative and over-admit jobs (subject was just "wip").

cases.query: Why is the pg driver pinned to a specific patch version instead of floating?
expectedEvidence: Commit message: pg 8.11.4/8.11.5 leak a pooled connection when an advisory-lock query fails; pinned to the last known-good 8.11.3. The change itself only touches a lockfile snapshot.

cases.query: Why is esbuild pinned to an older version instead of tracking latest?
expectedEvidence: Commit message: esbuild 0.19.3/0.19.4 mis-handle backslash path separators on Windows, breaking Windows CI; 0.19.2 is the last good version before the regression.

cases.query: We had some kind of special handling for Safari and cookies -- was that ever needed, and is it still there?
expectedEvidence: Introduced: Safari 12.0-12.1 drops SameSite=None+Secure cookies; omit SameSite for those versions.
Removed: traffic from Safari 12.0-12.1 under 0.01% for two quarters and those versions are unsupported; workaround deleted.

cases.query: Why did we widen the token expiry buffer for the Globex client specifically?
expectedEvidence: Commit message: Globex documents up to 60s of clock skew across their auth cluster; 30s buffer was not enough margin.

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: Treat Acme 200 responses with an error field as failures
whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.reason: A different provider (Acme) with an unrelated response-shape quirk, not a token-expiry buffer change.

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: Never retry Initech 501 responses
whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.reason: A different provider (Initech) with an unrelated status-code semantics issue.

cases.query: Why does SocketPool track sockets in each room with a Set instead of a WeakSet?

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: Fix duplicate message dispatch after reconnect
whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.reason: Touches SocketPool's Set usage but only to guard against duplicate add(); never discusses Set vs. WeakSet.

cases.query: Why is the worker pool size configurable but the queue's maximum backlog is not?
Why did we pick NDJSON specifically instead of, say, Parquet for the streaming export format?

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: Replace in-memory CSV export with streaming NDJSON
whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.reason: Explains why streaming replaced in-memory building (an OOM at ~4M rows), but never compares NDJSON to other streaming formats.

cases.query: Why was esbuild chosen as the bundler for this project in the first place, rather than swc or Rollup?

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: Pin esbuild to 0.19.2 pending a Windows path-handling fix
whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.reason: Explains a version pin, not the original choice of esbuild as the bundler.
